title: Learned serum profiles separate sampled cardiac and control infants
summary: In a study of 52 infants with single-ventricle heart disease and 48 controls, random-forest analysis distinguished circulating metabolite profiles, reporting a 7.49% error and separate leave-one-out group discrimination. This represents an exploratory multivariate sample pattern, not an established diagnostic test or an AI discovery of the reported metabolic pathways.

source_review.scope: Actual relevant original clinical/computational Methods and Results read;111 original v1 and later journal checked separately; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: A fitted forest learns group-discriminating patterns from relative metabolite abundances and ranks features by permutation importance. Conventional differential/pathway analyses and univariate outcome trends are separate.
evidence.tested: The source describes random-forest group classification, out-of-bag-style error reporting and leave-one-out evaluation on the sampled infant cohorts. The represented case/control comparison uses the existing metabolomic measurements.
evidence.unknown: Cases and controls differ in age and blood-sampling site; medication, support and surgical context can confound profiles. Exact patient-level containment across repeated/multiple-site samples is not fully established in the reviewed model description. Clinical-outcome metabolite associations did not survive multiplicity correction and are not adopted. Relative measurements and one high-altitude centre limit transfer. The linked editorial is authenticated by primary metadata, but its body was not reviewed. No causal pathway, postoperative benefit or independently replicated clinical test is claimed.
